# Two Emissions Tracks in the Acid Rain Program

Under Title IV, the Acid Rain Program addressed sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides from the power sector through different mechanisms. In its sulfur dioxide system, each covered allowance represented permission for one ton of emissions under an aggregate cap, with allowances traded among participants. The cap set a permitted total; it was not a measure of reported actual emissions.

Sulfur dioxide coverage expanded in phases. Phase I began in 1995 with 263 initial units at 110 plants. Substitution or compensating units brought the Phase I total to 445 units. Phase II began in 2000, and the final cap, reached in 2010, was 8.95 million tons.

The nitrogen oxides component followed a separate track for certain coal-fired units. It began in 1996 and used a rate-based approach, without a cap or allowance trading. The two pollutants therefore had distinct regulatory mechanisms and timelines.
